reviews.text: PDSA looked after my previous dog for a few years, right up until I had to put him to sleep. The staff were beyond compassionate. We were in the building long after they closed for the evening and we were never rushed out the door. They answered all my questions, the looked after my boy and treated him with dignity and respect. They now care for my current dog and again with the same compassion, care and respect. The prices are incredibly reasonable for Vet fees and medication. Incredibly grateful to the staff there.

Four years ago we had an emergency with my mums cat. Turned out he was suffering and needed put to sleep. NEVER EVER let them put your animal to sleep. Two women arrived one with a massive needle filled with Green liquid and they ruby tackled him and rammed the big fat needle up his leg. He died SCREEAMING. Then they asked if I wanted a minute with him. There was two door in the room and both self locked I think. After ten mins of saying goodbye again I couldn’t get out the room and strangely he started to smell. I was banging on both doors trying to get out. Had to speak to another customer through the door to get help to get out. NEVER EVER AGAIN. He died I AGONY. Heartless heartless ending for a beautiful boy. I’ll never forget how I let him down on his final moments trusting he was going to be on.

UPDATE: 03/24

Since writing my 1st review, I've had the misfortune of my dog being ill and having to take her to the PDSA again, with two visits being emergencies. I cannot praise this practice enough!  These people are amazing. I wish I had the funds to donate the actual cost of a consultation, I try to donate what I can afford each visit.

Wasn't sure what to expect as this was the first time having to use the PDSA. They are such lovely people from the receptionists to the Vet and the people who work in medication dispensing. They are patient, helpful, polite and put me at ease.The waiting room was very busy but I never felt like I was being rushed through, the Vet took the time to explain what was wrong with my dog, why it happens and answered my questions. She prescribed some medication which has definitely helped.

If you need to use the PDSA please donate what you can, it doesn't have to be a lot anything is better than nothing and I'm sure they'd be grateful. 🐕‍🦺🐕
